stage_a.note: Founders smile often, use energetic gestures, and enthusiastically joke with the panel using photos.
They show sustained excitement for their chocolate milk revolution with animated delivery.
They are highly approachable and friendly, complimenting the sharks and inviting them to join.

venture.description: A lower-sugar, higher-protein, lactose-free chocolate milk designed for adults and packaged in shelf-stable cans.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders introduce Slate as a lower-sugar, higher-protein, lactose-free chocolate milk for adults and invite the sharks to try it.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: They prepare to hand out samples and confirm it is lactose-free.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: He clarifies that the can shown is just a prototype.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: He asks to confirm that having a prototype implies they are pre-sales.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: He confirms they are.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: He remarks on the four million dollar valuation with no revenue.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: She asks to receive the samples.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: He asks which flavor they should taste first.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: He instructs them to try the dark chocolate first.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: He explains the dark chocolate targets the dairy alternative drinker.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: He makes a negative physical reaction to the taste.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: He bluntly states he does not like the taste at all.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: He asks S3 if he normally eats dark chocolate.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: He confirms that he does eat dark chocolate.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: He jokes that seeing S3 hate it makes him like it more.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: She notes she prefers the classic flavor over the dark.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: He says the classic should remind her of childhood chocolate milk.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: She points out a distinct dryness after swallowing.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: He describes a funky taste but hopes it serves as a major alternative calorie option.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: He affirms it is, citing 75 percent less sugar, 130 calories, and 9 grams of sugar per can.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: He asks why the product is so big.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: He explains they are playing on the consumer trend of decreasing sugar and increasing protein.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: He asks what it costs to make the product.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: He states it costs 85 cents to make.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: He asks for the selling price to distributors.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: He answers a dollar seventy-seven, noting the margin.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: She asks what the retail price will be.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: He tells her it will be 2.99.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: She asks to confirm they haven't produced the product yet since it's a prototype.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: He clarifies they have completed a pilot run.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: She challenges the high valuation given their early stage.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: He agrees and demands they address the valuation directly.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: He challenges them to defend the valuation before he eviscerates them.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: She calls the valuation absurd and asks what they were thinking.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: He jokes that having two good-looking founders is a huge part of the valuation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: He explains they have a third partner who successfully grew a Greek yogurt company to massive sales.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: He questions if that partner justifies the four million dollar valuation.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: He adds the partner has invested in other successful businesses and acts as their VP of sales.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: He asks if they even need a shark given this partner.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: She challenges the logic that his past success makes their new business worth that much.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: He dismisses their reasoning as a non-sequitur that makes no sense.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: He defends the valuation by citing the partner's relationships, which got them in front of four major retailers.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: She counters that connections don't matter if people don't like the product.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: He argues that it is ultimately about profits, which they do not have.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: She reiterates that asking for an enormous price based on an unknown partner is unreasonable.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: He mocks their logic, saying his own relationships would make him worth four billion.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: He acknowledges they are at the starting line but defends what they have built.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: He warns them they will be crushed and says they are further from four million than when they entered.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: She asks if they realize how weird it sounds to ask for money on a wish and a prayer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: He concedes that they probably framed their current position incorrectly.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: She states that they are just too early without sales and goes out.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: He asks if they have already raised any money.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: He confirms they have raised about two hundred thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: He asks what valuation that money was raised at.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: He says it was around a four million dollar valuation a year ago.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: He mishears and asks if they sold half the company for two hundred thousand.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: He corrects him, stating it was fifteen percent, and the partner also gives ten hours a week.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: He challenges them on expecting the sharks to pay ten times more than their sales partner.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: He confidently affirms that they do expect that.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: He sharply criticizes their lack of progress and taste, says he is holding back, and goes out.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: He thanks S5 and notes they have done over a hundred iterations on the taste.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: She explains they provided no proof of consumer taste tests and are asking for money based on a plan, so she is out.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: He references his initial negative reaction to the taste and says he doesn't love it, so he is out.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: He commends their energy but states his gut feeling on the product is not there, so he is out.

decisions.note: They are too early and have no sales.
The product does not taste good enough and they are nothing yet.
No proof of taste tests and asking for money on just a business plan.
He does not love the taste.
His gut feeling on the product is negative.

claim_conflicts.note: Founder states a $400k (or $4M) valuation, then says $200k bought 15%, implying $1.33M.

record.notes: F2's statement at 5:54 sounds like 'four million' but S3 interprets it as a math problem based on a lower valuation. The claims conflict mathematically.
